poem:
## The Lost-Wax Sprue Tree

'Twas brillig, and the waxen blobs
Did gyre and gimble in the sand;
All gooey were the moulden throbs,
And the sprue-tree out of hand.

"Beware the Sprue-Tree, oh my son!
The branches rough, the pour-holes deep!
Beware the draggle-cast, and shun
The Snarling Shrinkage-Creep!"

He took his melta-blade in hand:
Long time the faulty foe he sought—
So rested he by the Flask-block stand,
And stood awhile in thought.

And, as in polished thought he stood,
The Sprue-Tree, with its sprut-sprut sound,
Came whiffling through the grimy wood,
And burbled as it wound!

One, two! One, two! And through and through
The melta-blade went snicker-snack!
He left it dead, and with its crew
He went galumphing back.

"And hast thou slain the Sprue-Tree foe?
Bring forth the ingot, oh my beam!
O frabjous day! Callooh! Callay!"
He chortled in his dream.

'Twas brillig, and the waxen blobs
Did gyre and gimble in the sand;
All gooey were the moulden throbs,
And the sprue-tree out of hand.
